intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that nanophthalmos-4 (NNO4) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TMEM98 gene on chromosome 17q11.

checks.claim: Nanophthalmos-4 (NNO4) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TMEM98 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Testing the Mariana Islands pedigree for TMEM98 mutations identified a 34 bp heterozygous deletion that spans the 3' end of exon 4 in all affected family members.
checks.explanation: Paper reports TMEM98 mutations (heterozygous deletion, His196Pro) in autosomal dominant nanophthalmos; NNO4 label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The TMEM98 gene is located on chromosome 17q11.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation in TMEM98 in a large white kindred with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos linked to 17p12-q12.
checks.explanation: Paper places TMEM98 in the 17p12-q12 linkage region; 17q11 is standard locus nomenclature within that region.

paragraphs.text: Nanophthalmos is a rare developmental disorder of the eye in which the globe is abnormally small but has no other major structural malformation. Short axial length leads to high hyperopia. The sclera is often thickened, and patients are at increased risk of angle-closure glaucoma and of complications after intraocular surgery, such as uveal effusion. Nanophthalmos-4 is the autosomal dominant form caused by mutation in TMEM98.

checks.claim: Nanophthalmos is a rare developmental disorder of the eye.
checks.evidence_quote: Simple microphthalmia (OMIM 309700), which refers to a structurally normal but small eye globe, is an uncommon congenital or developmental ocular anomaly.
checks.explanation: The paper describes simple microphthalmia, not nanophthalmos by name.

checks.claim: In nanophthalmos, the globe of the eye is abnormally small but has no other major structural malformation.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal dominant nanophthalmos is an inherited eye disorder characterized by a structurally normal but smaller eye.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: In nanophthalmos, short axial length leads to high hyperopia.
checks.evidence_quote: it is usually bilateral with a short axis and has hyperopia of +7.00 to +13.00 diopters
checks.explanation: Stated for simple microphthalmia; the paper also attributes hyperopia to the short ocular axis. It does not use the term nanophthalmos.

checks.claim: In nanophthalmos, the sclera is often thickened.
checks.evidence_quote: Nanophthalmic eyes also have thick and impermeable sclera
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients with nanophthalmos are at increased risk of angle-closure glaucoma.
checks.evidence_quote: with the main complications being severe hyperopia and angle-closure glaucoma
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: Patients with nanophthalmos are at increased risk of complications after intraocular surgery, such as uveal effusion.
checks.evidence_quote: which has been associated with a high risk of developing choroidal effusions after any intraocular surgery.
checks.explanation: Choroidal effusion is a form of uveal effusion.

checks.claim: Nanophthalmos-4 is the autosomal dominant form of nanophthalmos caused by mutation in TMEM98.
checks.evidence_quote: To our knowledge, this represents the first gene identified causing autosomal dominant nanophthalmos.
checks.explanation: Stated.

paragraphs.text: Awadalla et al. (2014) found that nanophthalmos in the families they studied segregated as an autosomal dominant trait.

checks.claim: In the families studied by Awadalla et al. (2014), nanophthalmos segregated as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: To perform a clinical and genetic investigation of a large white family with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos.
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant inheritance described for one family (NNO-SA1); inheritance in additional families not reported.

paragraphs.text: Nanophthalmos is genetically heterogeneous. Both autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive forms have been described, including the recessive form caused by mutation in the MFRP gene.

checks.claim: Nanophthalmos is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Nanophthalmos has a strong genetic basis, and autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive forms of inheritance have been reported.
checks.explanation: Multiple genes (MFRP, TMEM98) and inheritance modes are described, which shows the condition is genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: Both autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive forms of nanophthalmos have been described.
checks.evidence_quote: Nanophthalmos has a strong genetic basis, and autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive forms of inheritance have been reported.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: An autosomal recessive form of nanophthalmos is caused by mutation in the MFRP gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Several cases of recessive nanophthalmos have been attributed to mutations in the MFRP gene.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Awadalla et al. (2014) studied families with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos. In affected members, they identified heterozygous mutations in the TMEM98 gene, which encodes a transmembrane protein, and the mutations segregated with the disease.

checks.claim: Awadalla et al. (2014) studied families with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos.
checks.evidence_quote: To perform a clinical and genetic investigation of a large white family with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos.
checks.explanation: Focus is one large family; additional families were screened but their inheritance pattern is not specified.

checks.claim: Awadalla et al. (2014) identified heterozygous mutations in the TMEM98 gene in affected members of families with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified a single novel segregating missense variant within the linkage region located in exon 8 of the transmembrane-98 (TMEM98) gene c.577G>C (p.Ala193Pro)
checks.explanation: A single variant in one family; mutations in other families and heterozygosity are not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: The TMEM98 gene encodes a transmembrane protein.
checks.evidence_quote: located in exon 8 of the transmembrane-98 (TMEM98) gene
checks.explanation: Gene name implies transmembrane protein; protein function not explicitly described.

checks.claim: The TMEM98 mutations identified by Awadalla et al. (2014) segregated with nanophthalmos in the families.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified a single novel segregating missense variant within the linkage region
checks.explanation: Segregation shown in family NNO-SA1 only, not multiple families.

paragraphs.text: Later mouse studies suggested that TMEM98 interacts with MYRF, another gene involved in nanophthalmos, and linked both proteins to ocular growth.

checks.claim: Mouse studies suggested that TMEM98 interacts with MYRF.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. No mouse studies, TMEM98 or MYRF are mentioned.

checks.claim: MYRF is a gene involved in nanophthalmos.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. MYRF is not mentioned in the paper.

checks.claim: Mouse studies linked both TMEM98 and MYRF proteins to ocular growth.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. No mouse studies or TMEM98/MYRF proteins are discussed.

references.label: Awadalla et al. (2014)
references.citation: Awadalla MS, Burdon KP, Souzeau E, Landers J, Hewitt AW, Sharma S, Craig JE. Mutation in TMEM98 in a large white kindred with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos linked to 17p12-q12. JAMA Ophthalmol 132: 970-7, 2014. [PubMed: 24852644]
